headlines.title: Dog attack leaves woman hospitalized with life-threatening injuries in SF
headlines.description: A woman was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries after being attacked by a large dog in San Francisco, police said. The incident was reported around 9:20 a.m. Tuesday on the 500 block of Larkin Street, in the city’s Tenderloin neighborhood just north of San Francisco City Hall. Police responded to the area for a report of a person being attacked by a dog. When officers arrived, they found an injured person and the attacking dog next to the victim, police said, adding officer separated the victim and dog. Police said officers restrained the dog until Animal Care and Control arrived to take it in custody. Video posted to the Citizen app show an officer yanking a dog away from the victim with a snare pole. Officer then immediately move in to help the woman. “Officers separated the victim and the dog,” police said in a news release. “Officers rendered aid to the victim and medics arrived on scene.” A witness said the dog had been wandering the streets off leash for a while before the attack. The dog is no longer alive, according to police. Anyone with information on the incident is asked to contact the SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD. headlines.title: Warming trend sparks heat advisory, Spare the Air alert in Bay Area
headlines.description: A heat advisory will be in effect for the Bay Area by midweek when rising temperatures are expected to peak. The National Weather Service said the heat advisory will start 10 am. Wednesday through 10 p.m. Thursday for the Bay Area and Central Coast. Temperatures are expected to range from 90-105 degrees in the interior, with the coast seeing mid-70s to low-90s. Meanwhile, the Bay Area Air Quality Management District has also issued a Spare the Air alert for Wednesday due to smog in the area. Authorities are asking motorists to limit their driving to reduce air pollution. Get your full Microclimate Forecast at nbcbayarea.com/weather. headlines.title: Pedestrian dies after being hit by vehicle in Fremont
headlines.description: A 60-year-old pedestrian died after being struck by a vehicle while walking in the middle of a road in Fremont early Monday morning. At about 4:15 a.m. Monday, Fremont police officers were sent an area of Stevenson Boulevard west of Marietta Drive to investigate reports of a collision involving a pedestrian. Police said the pedestrian was allegedly walking east on Stevenson near the center median and was hit. The driver stayed at the scene and cooperated with investigators, who don’t believe drugs or alcohol were a factor in the crash, police officials said Tuesday. The pedestrian was taken to the hospital, where they later died. Their name hasn’t been released. It was Fremont’s eighth fatal traffic collision this year on city streets. Anyone with information can contact the Fremont Police Department Traffic Unit at 510-790-6760, by texting ‘Tip FremontPD’ along with a short message to 888-777, or by visiting www.fremontpolice.gov/Tip.

headlines.title: How to watch 49ers vs. Rams NFL season opener in Australia on NBC Bay Area
headlines.description: The 49ers and Los Angeles Rams have descended upon Melbourne for the first-ever NFL game in Australia. The NFC West rivals begin their respective 2026 NFL seasons at 5:35 p.m. PT on Thursday, Sept. 10, at Melbourne Cricket Ground, which holds over 100,000 spectators. But if you didn’t make the trek to Melbourne, don’t worry. NBC Bay Area and NBC Sports Bay Area have you covered. Coverage begins at 4:30 p.m. with an NBC Bay Area special anchored in studio by Janelle Wang and Raj Mathai, with live reports from Australia from sports reporter Anthony Flores. NBC Bay Area will televise Netflix’s programming of the game beginning at 5 p.m. Kickoff is scheduled for 5:35 p.m. The matchup will make history as the NFL’s first regular season game played in Australia. Immediately following the game, NBC Bay Area will air Sports Sunday presented by Xfinity, featuring reaction and analysis from the 49ers’ season opener. NBC Sports Bay Area will also have you covered with “49ers Pregame Live” and “49ers Postgame Live,” featuring comprehensive reaction and analysis from the team, including Matt Maiocco reporting from Melbourne. Don’t miss a minute of the 49ers’ season-opener coverage across NBC Bay Area and NBC Sports Bay Area. headlines.title: ‘It's a privilege to be here': Giants voice Mike Krukow will sign off at the end of the month
headlines.description: It’ll be an emotional month for the San Francisco Giants family as one of their family members will be leaving. The Giants iconic voice Mike Krukow will officially sign off on Sept. 27, the team’s final game of the season. ‘Kruk and Kuip’ have been the voices and faces of the Giants for more than 40 years. We’ve known ‘Kruk and Kuip’ as players, broadcasters and always best friends. Mike Krukow says telling Duane he was retiring was one of the hardest things he’s ever had to do. Krukow says, “We’ve been through so much life together. I didn’t know if there was a perfect time or a perfect place …. and then in the end, it was just in the lunchroom, the two of us sitting there and I said, I think I’m done. He goes, no, you’re not. No, you are not, stop it. And I nodded my head, I think I am.” He goes on to say, “it got quiet. I was rolling down the hallway. He just put his arm on my shoulder. We didn’t say anything. We just walked in silence in the booth and sat down and got ready to do another game.” They are family in the NBC Sports Bay Area broadcast booth. Their passion for the game and friendship will never go away. But, Krukow says his health makes it unsafe to be doing the job. The 74-year-old suffers from inclusion body myositis, a degenerative muscle disease that’s forced him in a wheelchair. “I don’t want to leave and mother nature has her way … Once I announced the retirement, people feel an urgency to come to me and tell me thank you and let them know how much I meant to them. Do you know how powerful that is?” says Krukow. Mike Krukow will sign off on Sept. 27. The San Francisco Giants final game of the season against the LA Dodgers will be the final game of his hall of fame career. When we asked him what his message to the fans will be on that last day, Krukow told us he’ll tell people he’s happy and in a good place. “As sad as it is to end what has been the pride of not just myself, but my family. I’m going to tell them just how much they mean to me and my family on the last day. I don’t know if you can really convey it in words, but it will be conveyed in emotion, that I can guarantee.”
headlines.source: Raj Mathai, Christine Ni and Jeremy Carroll

headlines.title: BART says gate upgrades helping reduce crime, fare evasion a year later
headlines.description: BART officials say the transit agency’s new fare gates have contributed to a substantial drop in crime and helped recover millions of dollars in fares that otherwise may have been lost to evasion. BART held a news conference Tuesday marking the one-year anniversary of the next-generation fare gates being installed across all 50 stations. The taller gates are designed to make fare evasion more difficult than the older, shorter gates. BART Police Chief Kevin Franklin credited the new gates with helping deter crime across the rail system. According to BART, crimes against riders have dropped 67% from the end of 2024 through the end of the most recent quarter, while safety-related delays have fallen 47%. Franklin described the gates as a “force multiplier” for safety. BART also showed off a newer motor and gear assembly designed to allow the gates to open faster while maintaining their strength against fare evasion. The Bay Area Council estimates the new gates have generated roughly $10 million in fares that otherwise would have been lost to fare evasion. BART also said a recent survey found rider satisfaction at just over 91%, the highest level in the transit agency’s history.

headlines.title: 49ers fans head to Australia for season opener with surprise sendoff from Steve Young
headlines.description: Dozens of San Francisco 49ers fans boarded a flight at San Francisco International Airport heading to Melbourne, Australia, to cheer on the team in Thursday’s season opener against the Los Angeles Rams. Before departing on their 16-hour United Airlines flight, travelers were given a surprise sendoff by 49ers legend and Hall of Fame quarterback Steve Young, who wished them safe travels and shook hands with fans at the gate. “Niners fans always travel … just always is,” Young said. The unexpected appearance by one of the franchise’s greatest players set an enthusiastic tone for fans heading down under. “I never met him before … great way to start it off,” said Francisco Vera, a fan from San Jose who is traveling with his wife to celebrate their anniversary. Dwight Hall of Antioch shared a similar sentiment about meeting the former quarterback before boarding. “I felt great, this is once in a lifetime … honor to meet him and see him,” Hall said. The traveling fans will arrive in Australia a couple of days before kickoff, giving many of them time to take in sights around Melbourne before the 49ers face the Rams on Thursday.

headlines.title: Rally planned ahead of federal hearing over proposed Gilroy ICE facility
headlines.description: A federal judge in San Jose is expected to hear arguments Tuesday over an effort to temporarily block construction of a proposed ICE detention facility in Gilroy. People who live near the proposed facility and immigrant advocates are expected to rally ahead of the 2 p.m. hearing. Santa Clara County Jun 25 Santa Clara County Jun 11 California Attorney General Rob Bonta and Santa Clara County are seeking to block construction, arguing that the project violates several local and federal laws, including immigration and environmental protections. They also argue that the federal government failed to consult with state and county leaders before moving forward. Federal records show the government leased 24 acres of land for 20 years and contracted with a developer for the facility. NBC Bay Area’s Kris Sanchez has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: RV catches fire near West Oakland BART station
headlines.description: Firefighters responded to an RV fire at an encampment near the West Oakland BART station Tuesday morning, according to the Oakland Fire Department. The fire was reported at about 6:22 a.m. near Fifth and Kirkham streets, where one RV was burning. At least one dog was tied to the RV, and animal control was requested to the scene, fire officials said. It was not immediately known whether anyone was inside the RV when the fire started. Additional details about the fire were not immediately available. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

headlines.title: Foster City to discuss emergency response to condo fire
headlines.description: Residents displaced by a six-alarm condo fire in Foster City last month are expected to return to City Hall Tuesday to ask city leaders to declare a local state of emergency. Roughly 150 people who lived at the Sea Spray Lane condo complex were displaced by the fire. Residents are seeking a local emergency declaration, which could open the possibility of a state-level declaration and provide access to additional resources, including living expenses, tax benefits and help streamlining insurance claims. During a contentious City Council meeting last month, city leaders indicated they did not believe a local emergency declaration or a governor’s state of emergency was necessary at the time. City leaders said low-interest disaster loans would be a better way to provide financial assistance to displaced residents. NBC Bay Area’s Bob Redell has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Artists demand answers after murals painted over in San Francisco's Clarion Alley
headlines.description: A new fight to preserve a well-known Mission District landmark is underway after several murals were painted over in an alley between 17th and 18th streets and Mission and Valencia streets. Clarion Alley is known for the dozens of murals that fill the space. But the Clarion Alley Mural Project (CAMP) says it is heartbroken and furious after someone painted over several of those public art pieces on Aug. 24. “When something like that happens, it’s like really painful because you know the amount of hours it’s spent to design the mural,” said Nyia Luna, an artist with Graffiti Camp for Girls. Three murals were painted over with white paint, and a fourth was partially destroyed, prompting artists to demand answers and restitution. One of the destroyed works was painted this year by Luna and Graffiti Camp for Girls, a nonprofit that teaches young girls to create public art. After learning what happened, Luna spent more than six hours and about $100 to create a new piece. “It’s a community space, you know, people from around here, locals and then people from across the globe come here to see these murals,” Luna said. Witness and artist Doug Rhodes said he spotted a man rolling white paint over the art and confronted him. “I saw some guy rolling over the murals with white paint with a roller, and I told him to stop, and he said, ‘Oh, my boss told me to do this,'” Rhodes said. Rhodes eventually got the worker to stop. “It’s always infuriating when art gets destroyed out of ignorance,” Rhodes said. “That’s my reaction, like, come on guys, do some due diligence here. Don’t just paint over it.” CAMP representatives said they received no warning before the incident. In an email exchange, Makras Real Estate Group—the realty company associated with the property—said the property owner received a call regarding graffiti and sent a team to remove it. Makras stated they were unaware of the incident until CAMP alerted them. Ivy Jeanne, co-director of the Clarion Alley Mural Project, said the organization is looking into its options to help protect the art moving forward. “This project has been around since 1992, and we have built relationships over these decades with various landlords to paint murals,” Jeanne said. “So it’s very well established that there’s a mural project, and it’s known that that wasn’t graffiti.” Jeanne added that the project hopes to maintain its mission despite the setback. “There’s been over 900 murals, and they have a lot to do with social justice, equity, and so that’s what we hope,” Jeanne said. “We hope to continue to flourish as a project.” For people who work nearby, the loss extends beyond the physical paint on the walls. “A lot of the history of like activism and, you know, again just like having diversity,” said local worker Imani Outen. “I feel like just having those values kind of like painted over or just washed away is just, you know, kind of unfortunate and just disempowering to like the legacy that’s been built for what it’s known for.” Prior to the incident, CAMP had already launched a $35,000 fundraising campaign to mark its upcoming 35th year and support its ongoing efforts in the community.

headlines.title: Healdsburg jewelry store burglary suspect arrested near Sacramento
headlines.description: A suspect wanted in connection with a downtown Healdsburg jewelry store burglary was arrested following a multi-agency investigation, authorities announced Monday. Denis Gabriel Chitu, 30, was taken into custody in Citrus Heights after fleeing from a suspect vehicle, according to the Healdsburg Police Department. Officers initially responded Aug. 31 to a burglary that had just occurred at a jewelry store in downtown Healdsburg. A lone subject entered the store, stole thousands of dollars in jewelry, and fled the area, according to initial reports. Investigators later determined the same subject attempted to steal from an additional jewelry store elsewhere in Sonoma County. Following the report, officers launched an investigation that included a review of Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data, an examination of surveillance footage, and the authoring and service of search warrants. On Sept. 1, Healdsburg police officers apprehended Chitu in Citrus Heights with assistance from the Citrus Heights Police Department. While the stolen jewelry was not recovered, multiple items of evidence were located within the suspect vehicle. Chitu initially provided a false name before authorities verified his identity. He was found to have more than a half-dozen outstanding felony arrest warrants originating from jurisdictions across the country, police reported. Chitu is currently being held with no bail due to his outstanding warrants.
